answer: A stake-bonded registry makes every agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits: the cost grows linearly while the gain stays flat. Like an orchard where each tree is tagged and its umber soil tested before harvest, a new identity earns trust only after its bond ages and its work is checked by peers. An island of verified agents can simply refuse to settle with unbonded strangers, so a Sybil flood starves instead of spreading.
